synopsis: The glossary includes subset simulation in the booklet’s rare-event methods family; Chapter 9 describes these methods as deliberately oversampling dangerous conditions while estimating naturalistic rates, provided observations can be reweighted by the real-world-to-accelerated distribution ratio [f14161, f6846]. Subset simulation and multilevel splitting originate in structural reliability or, more broadly, reliability engineering, and are recommended for very small probabilities in structural reliability [f6855, f7272, f7269]. They can provide rate estimates through conditional levels, with academic tools identified as typical tooling [f7270, f7273]. However, both methods are described as weak for discontinuous perception responses, and their independent evidence base does not include any collision-avoidance application found by the booklet [f6856, f7271, f6857, f7274].
